CommandSpec.description:
One SCPI command: bound to a setting (``state``), to a component operation (``op``), or, through
its parameters' ``state``, to several settings at once.

args.description: Constant arguments passed to the operation
args.title: Args

factor.description: The command's number is the bound setting times factor: :TIMebase:RANGe is factor 10 on the time/div setting; a write divides by it
factor.title: Factor

read.description: An operation command's query reads this setting instead of calling the operation: 'OPER' enters operate, 'OPER?' reads it (the setting the operation writes)
read.title: Read

reply.description: Query reply template: {header} (the echoed header, see dialect.echo_header; with echo off it and the space after it are left out), {value} (the bound setting, or an operation's reply), {value_block} (that reply as an IEEE 488.2 definite-length block, e.g. '#13(@)') and {<setting>}, e.g. '{header} {value} V'. Default: '{header} {value}' for settings; an operation's reply as it is
reply.title: Reply

set_value.description: A setting command without parameters writes this constant and its query reads it back (LOCAL / REMOTE / LOCKOUT, which only set the interface state)
set_value.title: Set Value

state.description: State path bound to the command, e.g. 'ch.frequency'
state.title: State

suffixes.description: Allowed values of named header suffixes other than <ch> (#335), e.g. {hw: [1], n: [1]} for the SMA100B's [:SOURce<hw>]:AM<n>:STATe (one RF path, the first modulation channel); an omitted suffix counts as 1, any other value is -114

when.description: Use this command only when parameters have these values, e.g. {name: DATA_ARRAY_1}: several commands may share a header, told apart by a parameter (C1:INSPECT? "WAVEDESC"). A later command on the same header without `when` is the fallback: it runs for the other values and when the parameter is left out (:SYSTem:ERRor? [STRing], #602)
when.title: When

writes.description: Settings a multi-setting command writes along with its parameters, e.g. {sense.function: VOLT} for CONFigure:VOLTage:DC: the command header itself selects the function. Validated like a parameter and written before them (the parameters win). On an operation's command they are written before the operation runs (#308: MEASure:CURRent? selects the current function, as the instrument does)
writes.title: Writes

Fault.description:
A fault: on the link to an instrument, in an instrument, or in a component (architecture.md 5.5).

Link faults (``timeout``, ``disconnect``, ``garble``, ``latency``, ``busy``) act on every client's
SCPI traffic to ``instrument``. ``error`` queues an error code and ``trip`` switches the
instrument's outputs off with an error, both once. ``drift`` makes a component parameter
drift by ``drift_per_s`` (relative, per second of virtual time); ``hidden`` sets it to
``value``. Both are undone when the fault ends.

at_s.description: Virtual time to start; omitted: at once
at_s.title: At S

code.description: For error / trip: SCPI error code (default -300); for error it must be in the instrument's error table or the SCPI standard list unless a message is given
code.title: Code

component.description: For drift / hidden: '<instrument>/<component>' or a part's name, e.g. 'rc'
component.title: Component

count.description: Link faults: number of messages affected; error: how many times it is queued
count.title: Count

drift_per_s.description: For drift: relative change per second, e.g. 1e-4
drift_per_s.title: Drift Per S

duration_s.description: How long it lasts; omitted: until cleared
duration_s.title: Duration S

garble_rate.description: For garble: share of bytes corrupted
garble_rate.title: Garble Rate

latency_s.description: For latency: added to every message
latency_s.title: Latency S

param.description: For drift / hidden: the component parameter, e.g. 'r'
param.title: Param

remaining.description: Messages left for a counted link fault

ResponseFormat.description:
How query responses are written (real models, D42): numbers, booleans and enumerations.

The defaults are what ``sb-*`` instruments have always returned, e.g. ``+1.000000E+03``.

digits.description: Digits after the decimal point (nr3 mantissa, nr2); significant digits (general)
digits.title: Digits

enum.description: short: SIN; long: SINUSOID (upper case); as_defined: SINusoid, as in `options`
enum.title: Enum

error_code.description: Code in :SYSTem:ERRor? replies: plain: 0,"No error"; signed: +0,"No error"
error_code.title: Error Code

exponent_digits.description: nr3: digits of the exponent, e.g. E+03 is 2
exponent_digits.title: Exponent Digits

number.description: nr3: +1.000000E+03; nr2: +1000.000000; nr1: +1000 (rounded); engineering: 1E+3, 200E-3 (exponent a multiple of 3, shortest mantissa); si: 4.00000000MHz — `significant` digits with an SI prefix and `unit` (#289); general: C %g with `digits` significant digits, lowercase e and no trailing zeros, 2.3346669042e-09, 19.749698639 (#383)
number.title: Number

readings.description: Numbers a component answers (marker values, trace points, counter readings): component — each component's own digits (the default, what sb-* instruments return); format — written in this format like the settings, for a manual whose replies share one format (N9320B: 16 digits, #366). Components whose digits are a definition parameter (a meter's or trigger model's `digits`) keep that parameter
readings.title: Readings

significant.description: engineering with this many significant digits, signed and with exponent_digits: +40.0E+00 (3), +0.00000E+00 (6); a command's own format may set its own
significant.title: Significant

unit.description: number: si — the unit written after the prefix, e.g. Hz (default: the setting's)
unit.title: Unit

ResponseFormat.title: ResponseFormat

truncated.description: More events than returned (the first ones are returned)
truncated.title: Truncated

ScopeMeasurement.description:
One channel's automatic measurements on the record the screen shows (#280), taken by the
scope's own measurement rules, so they agree with its :MEASure? replies on the same record.
